children: Kuwait’s cabinet has approved a law amending certain provisions of its existing public tenders regulations with the aim of simplifying procedures.

The modified law also addresses difficulties and enhances the flexibility of relevant authorities in dealing with tender processing, thereby ensuring swift, efficient, transparent, and fair implementation of public tender procedures.

The amendments include increasing the value of oil contracts subject to procurement procedures to 20 million Kuwaiti dinars ($66 million), with the possibility of modifying this amount by a cabinet decision, according to the local media.
The Supreme Petroleum Council is granted the authority to authorise purchases, imports, or the assignment of urgent work to contractors, the report said.

They also include raising the financial limit for contracts under the jurisdiction of the Central Agency for Public Tenders (CAPT) to KWD 1 million ($3.3 million), with the possibility of increasing or decreasing this limit by the cabinet.

Tenders valued at less than KWD 1 million will be subject to the supervision of the relevant ministry, according to the new law which also includes reassessing the bases and criteria for classifying contracting companies.

The new regulations establish a new mechanism to determine the preference for national products, reducing the preference for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) from 20 percent to 10 percent, while prohibiting the combination of both preferences.
Contractors are also required to purchase at least 30 percent of the products listed in the local industrial directory.
(Writing by N Saeed; Editing by Anoop Menon)
